# Capri AI Gateway

> An intelligent, enterprise-grade AI microservice that connects Large Language Models to the Headless Digital Asset Management (DAM) ecosystem via the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

[![CI](https://github.com/ashok-pelluru/capri-ai-gateway/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ashok-pelluru/capri-ai-gateway/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Docker Build](https://github.com/ashok-pelluru/capri-ai-gateway/actions/workflows/docker.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ashok-pelluru/capri-ai-gateway/actions/workflows/docker.yml)
[![Security](https://github.com/ashok-pelluru/capri-ai-gateway/actions/workflows/security.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ashok-pelluru/capri-ai-gateway/actions/workflows/security.yml)
[![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11+-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)
[![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-0.115+-green.svg)](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/)
[![LangChain](https://img.shields.io/badge/LangChain-0.3+-orange.svg)](https://python.langchain.com/)
[![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-ready-blue.svg)](https://www.docker.com/)
[![License: Apache 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache_2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

---

## Overview

The **Capri AI Gateway** acts as the decoupled translation layer between LLMs and the core Rails DAM system. It provides:

- **MCP Server** – exposes DAM search tools via the Model Context Protocol so any AI agent can discover and invoke them
- **FastAPI REST API** – semantic embedding, AI-powered TDM provenance governance, and an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat` proxy
- **Redis Event Listener** – event-driven pipeline for real-time asset embedding and metadata transformation (auto-reconnecting)
- **Dynamic LLM Orchestration** – hot-swap between OpenAI, Anthropic, and Perplexity without restarting, with a local (Ollama) fallback
- **Enterprise guardrails** – `X-DAM-Gateway-Secret` auth, monthly budget caps (`402`), circuit breaker + retry, and Prometheus `/metrics`

### Endpoints

| Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/embed_query` | Text → dense embedding vector (`vector`, `model`, `tokens`) |
| `POST /api/tdm/evaluate` | TDM provenance gate (`tdm_safe`, `confidence`, `flags`, …) |
| `POST /v1/chat` | OpenAI-compatible chat completion (budget + circuit breaker) |
| `GET /health` | Provider/Redis health + uptime |
| `GET /metrics` | Prometheus metrics |

---

## Quick Start

```bash
# 1 – Clone and set up
git clone <repo-url>
cd capri-ai-gateway
python3.11 -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
make install

# 2 – Configure
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env and add your OPENAI_API_KEY at minimum

# 3 – Run (local)
make run-api          # FastAPI on :8000
make run-listener     # Redis listener (separate terminal)

# 3b – Run with Docker
docker compose up --build
```

API docs: http://localhost:8000/docs  
Health check: http://localhost:8000/health

---

## Project Structure

```
src/gateway/
├── api/          # FastAPI app, middleware (auth + metrics), route handlers
├── agents/       # Embedding, transformation, metadata extraction
├── core/         # Config, logging, LLM manager, metrics, retry
├── providers/    # Pluggable chat providers (base, local/Ollama, registry)
├── services/     # Circuit breaker, budget governance, chat router
├── schemas/      # Typed request/response models
├── listener/     # Redis pub/sub consumer + event handlers
└── mcp/          # Model Context Protocol server
```

import os
import httpx
import asyncio
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from mcp.server import Server
from mcp.server.stdio import stdio_server
from mcp.types import Tool, TextContent, CallToolResult

# Load environment variables from .env file
load_dotenv()

# Initialize the Model Context Protocol Server
app = Server("capri-mcp")

# Configuration via environment variables with sensible local defaults
DAM_API_BASE = os.getenv("DAM_API_BASE", "http://localhost:3000/api/v1")
DAM_API_TOKEN = os.getenv("DAM_API_TOKEN", "")

@app.list_tools()
async def list_tools() -> list[Tool]:
    """
    Exposes the available DAM tools to the connecting LLM application.
    AI agents parse this schema to discover capabilities and construct parameters.
    """
    return [
        Tool(
            name="search_assets",
            description=(
                "Search and filter digital assets within the Capri ecosystem. "
                "Use this tool when users look for images, files, or specific creative campaigns."
            ),
            inputSchema={
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "query": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "The search term or keyword matching asset titles or filenames (e.g., 'logo', 'banner')."
                    },
                    "mode": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "enum": ["images", "files"],
                        "default": "images",
                        "description": "The type constraint. Use 'images' for graphics/photos and 'files' for document formats like PDFs."
                    }
                },
                "required": ["query"]
            }
        )
    ]

@app.call_tool()
async def call_tool(name: str, arguments: dict) -> CallToolResult:
    """
    Executes the underlying asset engine tools when requested by the AI agent.
    Performs the HTTP translation between the MCP protocol and the Rails REST API.
    """
    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
            response = await client.get(
                f"{DAM_API_BASE}/search",
                params={"q": query},
                headers={"traceparent": incoming_trace_parent} # Forward the ID
            )

    if name != "search_assets":
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported tool execution requested: {name}")

    query = arguments.get("query")
    mode = arguments.get("mode", "images")

    # Set up secure communication headers with the primary Rails Monolith
    headers = {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "Accept": "application/json"
    }
    if DAM_API_TOKEN:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {DAM_API_TOKEN}"

    # Prepare HTTP query parameters matching our Rails SearchController API contract
    params = {
        "q": query,
        "mode": mode
    }

    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10.0) as client:
        try:
            # Dispatch asynchronous query to the decoupled search endpoint
            response = await client.get(f"{DAM_API_BASE}/search", params=params, headers=headers)

            # Bubble up HTTP errors gracefully without crashing the background MCP process
            response.raise_for_status()
            data = response.json()

            meta = data.get("meta", {})
            results = data.get("results", [])

            # Flatten the structural JSON API response into highly semantic, readable markdown
            # This serialization layout optimizes LLM token consumption and context reasoning accuracy
            content_summary = f"### DAM Search Summary\n"
            content_summary += f"Query: `{meta.get('query')}` | Mode: `{meta.get('mode')}`\n"
            content_summary += f"Total Records Found: **{meta.get('total_found', 0)}**\n\n"
            content_summary += "### Matching Assets\n"

            if not results:
                content_summary += "_No assets matched the specified filters._\n"
            else:
                for idx, asset in enumerate(results, 1):
                    content_summary += f"{idx}. **{asset.get('title')}**\n"
                    content_summary += f"   - **UUID:** `{asset.get('uuid')}`\n"
                    content_summary += f"   - **Mime-Type:** {asset.get('type')}\n"
                    content_summary += f"   - **File Size:** {asset.get('size')}\n"
                    content_summary += "   ---\n"

            return CallToolResult(
                content=[TextContent(type="text", text=content_summary)],
                isError=False
            )

        except httpx.HTTPStatusError as e:
            error_details = f"DAM API returned error code {e.response.status_code}: {e.response.text}"
            return CallToolResult(
                content=[TextContent(type="text", text=error_details)],
                isError=True
            )
        except httpx.RequestError as e:
            error_details = f"Network transport failure communicating with Capri: {str(e)}"
            return CallToolResult(
                content=[TextContent(type="text", text=error_details)],
                isError=True
            )

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Launch the server utilizing standard input/output streams (stdio)
    # This acts as the secure local IPC layer when spawned by the LangChain runtime
    async def main():
        async with stdio_server() as (read_stream, write_stream):
            await app.run(
                read_stream,
                write_stream,
                app.create_initialization_options()
            )

    asyncio.run(main())
